title: Voiding cystourethrogram in a child
what: Contrast is put into the bladder through a thin catheter, and X-rays are taken while your child pees. This shows whether urine flows back up to the kidneys.
why: Usually after urinary tract infections with fever, or if an ultrasound showed widened kidneys.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes, with the result the same day
tell_doctor: If your child has a urine infection or fever now
If your child has an allergy to contrast or medicines
If there is a latex allergy

prepare.title: Urine test
prepare.text: A fresh urine test showing no infection is often needed before the exam. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Antibiotic
prepare.text: Sometimes the doctor prescribes an antibiotic as a precaution. The doctor will give the plan.

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: Calmly explain to your child what will happen. You can bring a favorite toy.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually your child can eat as normal.

bring: A change of underwear and a diaper
A toy, or a cartoon on your phone
steps: Your child lies on the X-ray table
The genital area is wiped with antiseptic
A thin catheter with gel is passed through the urinary channel
The bladder is slowly filled with contrast through the catheter
Pictures are taken, then your child is asked to pee, and more are taken
feel: Placing the catheter is unpleasant and your child may cry
A strong urge to go to the toilet
Peeing while lying on the table can feel strange and awkward
after: Have your child drink more today
The first 1 or 2 times it may sting a little to pee
The report is usually the same day, and the doctor makes the decision
red_flags: Severe pain when peeing, or your child cannot pee
Blood in the urine for more than a day

faq.q: Can I stay with my child?
faq.a: Usually one parent can stay. You will be given a protective apron.
Backflow of urine is often seen exactly during peeing.

reminders.text: Your child's bladder X-ray exam is tomorrow. Bring the urine test, a change of underwear and a toy.
